pr_title: roachtest: refactor tests to use WorkloadNode spec
pr_body:
This change refactors roachtests to use the new WorkloadNode
cluster spec and the helpers that come with it. It also uses
smaller workload nodes for certain tests.

This change also removes unnecessary usage of the deprecated
workload, opting to use cockroach workload when possible.

Release note: none
Fixes: #62302

--------------
Sorry for the big diff, but most of the changes boil down to:

1. Switching `workload` to `cockroach workload` when possible.
2. Specifying `spec.WorkloadNodes` when a test uses a workload only node.
3. Using the new `c.WorkloadNodes` and `c.CRDBNodes` helpers instead of doing node arithmetic (i.e. `c.Range(1, c.NodeCount - 1)`

Smoke testing is a bit scattered between TC and local runs, but I made a [spreadsheet here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1kIE39psGmeaSxJdsQ_XaO9X5qAzvCrvFekyVJ0RdhcQ/edit?gid=0#gid=0) of all changed tests  and made sure there weren't any regressions in the case of using a smaller workload node.
pr_comments:
Your pull request contains more than 1000 changes. It is strongly encouraged to split big PRs into smaller chunks.

<sub>:owl: Hoot! I am a [Blathers](https://github.com/apps/blathers-crl), a bot for [CockroachDB](https://github.com/cockroachdb). My owner is [dev-inf](https://github.com/orgs/cockroachdb/teams/dev-inf).</sub>
This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/126506)

>if there are any examples where multiple workload nodes are used

`cdc/kafka-chaos-multiple-sink-nodes` is one such example I just added, which treats the sink nodes as "workload" nodes in the context of provisioning smaller vms.

Not 100% sure if I'll keep it though. The logic for determining if there's a workload node, if the workload node shares a node with the sink node, etc. already seems a bit complex, and I'm not sure if my refactor makes it better or worse. At the very least latency wise and cpu wise it seems fine though.

The large TPCC one was the main one I had in mind though 😄

> Not 100% sure if I'll keep it though. The logic for determining if there's a workload node, if the workload node shares a node with the sink node, etc. already seems a bit complex, and I'm not sure if my refactor makes it better or worse. 

Yeah, it's hard to say if the refactoring made the "setup" logic less complex; I'd say it's roughly what it was before. The complicating factor is that the framework doesn't really support having workload nodes interleaved with other types of non-cluster nodes. However, this test seems like a one-off. Unless we observe this pattern across other tests, it doesn't merit adding this new capability. Wrt refactoring, I'll let you decide if you want to keep it. Fwiw, I think it's slightly better than the previous version :)

> At the very least latency wise and cpu wise it seems fine though.

Yeah, I wouldn't worry about that since "setup" isn't on a critical path.

>However, this test seems like a one-off. Unless we observe this pattern across other tests, it doesn't merit adding this new capability.

Agreed, I've removed it from the PR. Looking at the TPCC draft PR, even that I don't think would need this feature since it just wants either multiple workload nodes OR custom vm cpu sizes. This feature would only be needed if you wanted both.

>Fwiw, I think it's slightly better than the previous version :)

Sounds good I've kept it then. Hopefully at least the comments help make it a bit more clear what's going on.

Thanks for taking a look Andy! Unfortunately I think most of your comments are outdated now that I've dropped the ability to have multiple workload nodes 😓 

For fun though, I'll try to explain the reasoning for going with a seemingly restrictive approach over a more elegant/comprehensive one like you suggested.

Ultimately, the value gained from this new `workloadNode` spec is just saving a couple dollars on cpu usage and removing a line or two of c.Range(1, c.Spec.NodeCount - 1), which IMO is a fairly low value win. With that in mind, I didn't want to overcomplicate the approach.

My initial solution was something closer to what you suggested, with the freedom to have multiple clusters specs per test. But I quickly realized that I was adding a lot of complexity to the roachprod cluster creation and to the cluster spec creation, just to satisfy the 1 or 2 tests that would actually use it.

The ability to have custom groupings of nodes via a `OtherNodes(label string)` would be nice, but in practice would just save one single test the need to do:

```
sinkNodes := c.Range(...)
```

So while only being compatible with 1 workload node, and forcing it to be the last node in the cluster seems restrictive, it covers *almost* every test. I do like your solution though, and will definitely keep it in mind if we do see more tests follow this pattern.

issue_context.title: roachtest: use smaller workload machines
issue_context.body:
When running a single-node roachtest workload, e.g. `kv95/enc=false/nodes=1/cpu=32`, two nodes are provisioned: one to run CRDB, and one to run the workload. However, both of these machines have the same specs, i.e. 32 CPUs, which seems excessive for the workload machine.

This can cause issues when running multiple tests in parallel, e.g. `--count 5`, since this ends up provisioning 320 CPUs while the default roachtest quota (as given by `--cpu-quota`) is 300. Not to mention the unnecessary cost. 💸

Jira issue: CRDB-2811
comments:

review_comments: Good riddance! Do we know why this parameterized by `numLoadNodes` even though the current implementation hardcodes `1`?
Not sure, I believe there were other cases of tests doing this. Perhaps future proofing?
